assignments.task_summary: Run a matched two-setting pool experiment and interpret queueing, failures and database work instead of selecting the largest throughput number.
Identify whether an unfamiliar slow owned-history run is dominated by allocation, acquisition wait or a locked query, and execute one discriminating counterexperiment.
Implement one operation deadline propagated through admission, database claim and mock-provider invocation, with an explicit unknown-result disposition.
Author the retry decision for one existing mock dispatch adapter and test known rejection, transport uncertainty and invalid input separately.
Implement a deadline-aware backoff schedule for safe retryable dispatch failures and verify it with a fake clock plus one bounded real-timer observation.
Implement one transactional admission rule for pending dispatch work so a full bounded queue rejects new work without losing already committed intent.
Write new regression tests for operation replay after response-cache expiry and for changed accepted input under a reused idempotency key.
Implement the existing operation-to-outbox seam in the owning transaction and fault it after each write boundary.
Author one database-backed batch-claim query and validate concurrent workers with deterministic barriers.
Implement one completion guard that checks the current durable claim token before committing a dispatch result.
Run an actual controlled application-worker stop/restart between committed intent and mock invocation, then verify the pending item is still claimable.

Execute a mechanism-disclosed guided recovery drill: the instructor states that the mock provider accepts p1 and the worker stops before local definitive SQL commit. Reproduce the resulting uncertainty, classify the surviving facts and author a no-blind-redelivery guard for the existing reconciliation path. This drill does not assess independent unfamiliar diagnosis.
Implement one existing reconciliation seam that consumes a mock observation for o1 and records a definitive result only when evidence supports it.
Implement one bulkhead between mock-provider work and local owned-history reads, then observe recovery after provider tasks stall.
Implement one shutdown sequence that stops new claims, bounds in-flight waiting and leaves unresolved operations durably recoverable.
Implement one ready-work selection rule that distinguishes request deadline expiry from durable operation recovery obligations.
Rebuild the bounded claim-and-complete seam from the public operation contract with the previous implementation hidden.
Execute one prepared durable-operation scenario combining overload and a lost response, then independently justify the terminal dispositions.
Implement validation for one existing local operating configuration boundary and expose a safe configuration fingerprint.
Implement one health/readiness boundary that distinguishes a running process from its ability to perform the required database-backed operation.
Author and execute one local start/stop wrapper using only reconciled existing controls, checking actual process identity and listening socket ownership.
Implement one structured incident log event linking request, operation and fault category through safe opaque diagnostic references.
Author a regression suite that forces validation, timeout and nested-exception paths through the existing logging boundary.
Implement one existing CI/local build gate that blocks candidate publication when the owned-history authorization regression fails.
Run the existing build twice from the same locked candidate and diagnose one prepared environment-dependent difference in its artifact manifest.
Implement one backward-compatible additive schema seam for a nullable safe diagnostic label and run old/new candidate compatibility checks.
Execute and verify one local application rollback from C1 to C0 against the expanded schema while retaining newly written compatible data.
Diagnose one prepared local application-to-database connectivity failure using process, listener and existing container/network observations.
Diagnose one intentionally mismatched archive/schema manifest and execute the restore preflight guard in a disposable target without decrypting data.
Execute one approved disposable-database backup and validate its actual manifest and authoritative record relationships while writes are controlled.
Exercise the existing approved teaching-key resolver before and after a controlled application process restart using one authorized encrypted canary.
Restore the retained bounded archive into an approved disposable target and verify recovered relationships and authorized content through the actual application.
Execute the prepared key-unavailable recovery mode and implement one guard against plaintext fallback or misleading empty-success behavior.
Rebuild the safe startup preflight from the operating contract with the earlier wrapper hidden, then run valid, occupied-port and incompatible-schema cases.
Implement one bounded local retention eligibility query for synthetic telemetry while protecting authoritative transaction and journey references.
Follow the reconstructed operating controls to recover one stopped disposable database dependency and verify the candidate rather than rehearsing every incident at once.
Record one production-build history-view interaction and correlate render commits, local requests and visible completion under the fixed browser fixture.
Implement one owner-scoped query-key/options factory that excludes incidental render state while retaining every server-result-changing filter.
Implement one targeted rendering optimization for the measured summary-row or derivation seam and compare matched traces.
Implement one query cancellation/late-result guard for rapid filter changes while maintaining an accessible truthful loading state.
Implement one measured local expensive-label preview boundary so input state stays immediate while the derived preview may lag explicitly.
Reuse the same typed query options across the page and its safe summary composition, then test request deduplication and failure recovery.
Author regression tests for focus, announcements and narrow-layout behavior after the selected rendering and fetch changes.
Add one lazy-loading boundary around a nonessential safe history explanation panel and verify chunk failure recovery.
Validate one finite Tailwind variant set in the production build after the panel split and repair a prepared missing-style boundary.
Measure and test one private query-cache lifecycle boundary during repeated navigation and account changes.
Author and execute the contract for a removable in-process public-catalog projection alternative to repeated derivation, using an executable counterexample before implementation.
Implement one bounded in-process public derivation cache behind the existing projection interface with the reference implementation preserved.
Implement one per-key single-flight seam for the bounded public projection adapter and test concurrent failure cleanup.
Run the retained public reference and optional adapter under matched local request mixes, measuring both hit-heavy and version-churn cases.
